teaching_point: PV: flaccid blisters that rupture almost at once, leaving raw erosions. Case 1 says 'no blisters', which is typical, because the roof is too thin to survive.
dermnet_caption: Erosions and flaccid blisters in pemphigus vulgaris

teaching_point: PV: widespread crusted erosions on the trunk. With fluid loss and poor oral intake (Case 1 hypovolaemia) this needs same-day admission under dermatology.
dermnet_caption: Eroded plaques in pemphigus vulgaris over the trunk
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Eroded plaques in pemphigus vulgaris over the trunk (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/pemphigus-vulgaris-images

teaching_point: Oral PV: painful buccal/palatal erosions, often the first sign and present for weeks before skin lesions. Anti-desmoglein 3 dominant. Mouth ulcers lasting more than 3 weeks need referral.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Oral pemphigus vulgaris (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/pemphigus-vulgaris-images

teaching_point: Chronic lip erosion in PV: easily mistaken for herpes labialis or angular cheilitis. Ask about other mouth ulcers and weight loss.
dermnet_caption: Chronic lip erosion in pemphigus vulgaris
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Chronic lip erosion in pemphigus vulgaris (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/pemphigus-vulgaris-images

teaching_point: Histology: suprabasal intraepidermal split with acantholysis. Basal cells stay attached to the basement membrane ('row of tombstones'). See Module 4 exam Q5.
dermnet_caption: Suprabasal intraepidermal blister formation with acantholytic keratinocytes and
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Suprabasal intraepidermal blister formation with acantholytic keratinocytes and (© Dr Richard Ashton) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/pemphigus-vulgaris-images

teaching_point: Direct immunofluorescence of perilesional skin: intercellular IgG in a 'fishnet/chicken-wire' pattern. Compare with linear BMZ in BP (B-series) and granular papillary IgA in DH (C05).
dermnet_caption: Direct immunofluorescence of perilesional skin in pemphigus vulgaris - immunostaining with IgG producing intercellular
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Direct immunofluorescence of perilesional skin in pemphigus vulgaris - immunostaining with IgG producing intercellular (© Dr Richard Ashton) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/pemphigus-vulgaris-images

teaching_point: Pemphigus foliaceus: superficial (subcorneal) scaly, crusted 'cornflake' erosions on the seborrhoeic trunk/face, with no mucosal disease (anti-Dsg1 only). Often misdiagnosed as impetigo or seborrhoeic dermatitis.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pemphigus foliaceus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/pemphigus-foliaceus

teaching_point: Drug-induced pemphigus (usually foliaceus pattern): thiol drugs such as penicillamine and captopril, and less often other ACE inhibitors or penicillins. Case 1 is taking ramipril, so record it and flag it, but it is a weak association.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Drug-induced pemphigus foliaceus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/drug-induced-pemphigus

teaching_point: BP: large tense, clear, intact bulla. The subepidermal split gives a full-thickness roof, so it survives. Older adult; itch dominant.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Bullous pemphigoid (© Raimo Suhonen) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/bullous-pemphigoid-images

teaching_point: Non-bullous (urticarial/eczematous) BP phase: itchy urticated plaques for weeks to months before blisters. Suspect BP in any elderly person with new itchy 'eczema' or 'hives' that fails to settle.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Bullous pemphigoid (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/bullous-pemphigoid-images

teaching_point: BP: tense clear and haemorrhagic blisters on an urticated base (Module 4 exam Q28). Check the drug history for DPP-4 inhibitors (gliptins), loop diuretics and checkpoint inhibitors.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Bullous pemphigoid (© Raimo Suhonen) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/bullous-pemphigoid-images

teaching_point: Widespread BP with many blisters and erosions: inability to self-care, infection or failing intake means same-day dermatology/medical assessment. Frailty matters (Formative quiz patient aged 85).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Bullous pemphigoid (© Raimo Suhonen) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/bullous-pemphigoid-images

teaching_point: Mucous membrane pemphigoid: desquamative gingivitis/oral erosions with scarring tendency. Distinguish from oral PV by biopsy and DIF. Needs dermatology plus oral medicine.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Gingival erosions due to MMP (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/mucous-membrane-pemphigoid

teaching_point: Ocular MMP: conjunctival scarring (symblepharon) can lead to blindness. Gritty or red eyes in a patient with blistering disease need urgent ophthalmology.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Conjunctival symblepharon due to MMP (© Dr Richard Ashton) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/mucous-membrane-pemphigoid

teaching_point: Pemphigoid gestationis: periumbilical urticated plaques then tense blisters in the 2nd/3rd trimester or postpartum. Refer urgently to dermatology and the obstetric team; it can recur in later pregnancies or with the COC.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pemphigoid gestationis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/pemphigoid-gestationis

teaching_point: DH classical distribution: elbows, sacrum and buttocks, symmetrical (Case 2 and Case 4). Intense itch or burning, so vesicles are often scratched away before you see them.
dermnet_caption: Elbow, sacral and buttock lesions - the classical distribution of dermatitis herpetiformis
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Elbow, sacral and buttock lesions - the classical distribution of dermatitis herpetiformis (© Dr Richard Ashton) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dermatitis-herpetiformis

teaching_point: Clustered ('herpetiform') excoriated vesicles on the elbow. The name refers to the grouping; there is no herpesvirus involved.
dermnet_caption: Clustered vesicles have been excoriated on the elbows in dermatitis herpetiformis
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Clustered vesicles have been excoriated on the elbows in dermatitis herpetiformis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dermatitis-herpetiformis

teaching_point: Excoriated vesicles on the buttocks and sacrum. Case 2 (30-year-old with 'IBS' and pallor). Check tTG-IgA with total IgA while the patient is still eating gluten.
dermnet_caption: Excoriated vesicles on the buttocks and sacrum in dermatitis herpetiformis
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Excoriated vesicles on the buttocks and sacrum in dermatitis herpetiformis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dermatitis-herpetiformis

teaching_point: Excoriations only, with no intact blisters: Case 4 (38-year-old, Betnovate failed, 'IBS' bloating). Potent TCS does not control DH. Think coeliac and do not keep escalating steroids.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Excoriated plaques in dermatitis herpetiformis (© Dr Richard Ashton) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/dermatitis-herpetiformis-images

teaching_point: DIF of perilesional (uninvolved) skin: granular IgA in the dermal papillae, which is diagnostic of DH. The biopsy must be taken from perilesional, not blistered, skin.
dermnet_caption: Granular deposits of IgA shown on direct immunofluorescence of perilesional skin (courtesy of Dr Richard Groves, London)
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Granular deposits of IgA shown on direct immunofluorescence of perilesional skin (courtesy of Dr Richard Groves, London) (© St John’s Institute for Dermatology) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dermatitis-herpetiformis

teaching_point: PCT: tense/haemorrhagic blisters, erosions and scars on the dorsal hands (Case 3, a homeless man with alcohol dependence and facial hypertrichosis).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Porphyria cutanea tarda (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/blistering-skin-conditions

teaching_point: Pseudoporphyria: PCT-like fragility and blisters with NORMAL porphyrins. Naproxen/NSAIDs, tetracyclines, furosemide, sunbeds and dialysis (Module 5 exam Q2). This is the pharmacist's catch.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pseudoporphyria (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/pseudoporphyria

teaching_point: Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita: trauma-site blisters, milia and scars that mimic PCT, but with no photosensitivity. Anti-type VII collagen. Needs specialist DIF/serology.
dermnet_caption: Blisters milia and scars due to EBA - they may mimic porphyria cutanea tarda
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Blisters milia and scars due to EBA - they may mimic porphyria cutanea tarda (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/epidermolysis-bullosa-acquisita

teaching_point: TEN: sheet-like epidermal detachment, Nikolsky positive, more than 30% BSA (Module 4 exam Q27, carbamazepine at 1 month). Stop the drug, 999/same-day to a burns-capable or dermatology unit, and report on a Yellow Card.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Toxic epidermal necrolysis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/stevens-johnson-syndrome-toxic-epidermal-necrolysis

teaching_point: SJS: dusky atypical targets and blisters with 2 or more mucosal sites, under 10% BSA. Prodrome of fever and sore eyes. High-risk drugs are carbamazepine, lamotrigine, allopurinol, sulfonamides, nevirapine and oxicam NSAIDs.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Stevens Johnson Syndrome (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/stevens-johnson-syndrome-toxic-epidermal-necrolysis

teaching_point: Bullous fixed drug eruption: recurs at the SAME site with each exposure and leaves dusky brown pigmentation. Ask about intermittent drugs (NSAIDs, paracetamol, co-trimoxazole, tetracyclines). Generalised bullous FDE can mimic SJS/TEN.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Blistering fixed drug eruption (© Raimo Suhonen) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/fixed-drug-eruption

teaching_point: AGEP: sheets of tiny sterile pustules on red skin, often flexural, within 1 to 5 days of starting a drug (beta-lactams, macrolides, diltiazem, hydroxychloroquine). Fever and neutrophilia. Stop the drug and get a same-day dermatology opinion.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis (AGEP) (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acute-generalised-exanthematous-pustulosis

teaching_point: Linear IgA disease: annular 'string of beads' / 'cluster of jewels' blisters. Drug-induced in adults, classically by vancomycin, also by ACE inhibitors and NSAIDs. Linear IgA on DIF. Dapsone-responsive.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — String of beads sign (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/linear-iga-bullous-disease

teaching_point: Hailey-Hailey (benign familial pemphigus): flexural, macerated, fissured erosions; family history. Acantholysis with NEGATIVE immunofluorescence (Hailey-Hailey, Darier and Grover).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Hailey-Hailey disease blisters (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/hailey-hailey-disease

teaching_point: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome: superficial (granular-layer) peeling, mainly in young children, with NO mucosal involvement. Distinguish from TEN, which involves mucosa and full-thickness epidermis. Same-day paediatric admission.
dermnet_caption: Superficial blistering over the axillae, face and chest due to staphylococcal scalded skin sydrome
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Superficial blistering over the axillae, face and chest due to staphylococcal scalded skin sydrome (© Dr Lawrence Meyerson) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/staphylococcal-scalded-skin-syndrome
